Is there a way to structure code such a way that we can add support for Inventory items contained by chassis (M) and Control Interfaces (N) by just doing M + N implementation instead of M*N.

The root cause is that one Control resource's data is split across two interfaces: Control.OperatingClockSpeed (SetPoint/SettingMax/Min/ControlMode — uniform per control type, the N axis) and the controlled inventory item (AllowableMax/Min + PhysicalContext, currently read from Item.Accelerator's MaxSpeedInHz/MinSpeedInHz/Type — the M axis). 
The only genuine M×N coupling is reading the allowable range from the inventory item, since each inventory type stores it under different properties. I think the cleanest fix is to expose the allowable range on Control.OperatingClockSpeed itself (add MaxSpeedInHz/MinSpeedInHz there); then bmcweb reads every control value from the control object (pure N) and the inventory item is only used to build the RelatedItem URI, which is a pure data table (pure M) — true M+N. I'd propose doing that as a follow-up PDI + dbus-sensors change. WDYT?
Sounds good.

The `locked` deterministic logic here looked wierd.
Based on my understanding, `presentSpeedLimit...` reflects only the applied limit on the devices, matching `presentSpeedLimitMinHz` and `presentSpeedLimitMaxHz` might not be enough to determine if the device is in disabled mode.

I think we can implement ControlMode at the `dbus-sensors` side to prevent the complicated logic here. 
However, that might requires modification on PDI because currently there is only a boolean flag differentiating manual and automatic mode.

PDI: 
https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Control/Mode.interface.yaml

bmcweb JSON schema: https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/6dd6f276a2dc8a7bd293b417e1a710ecd987c9fc/redfish-core/schema/dmtf/json-schema/Control.v1_8_0.json#L606

I think we can move this part to the upper function stack. 

Conceptually, we perform O(M) searching for corresponding inventory item.
After that, by using the matched inventory item we then perform O(N) interfaces walk through to retrieve the desired properties.

Your current implementation is indeed using this approach, but however, in a confusing approach because the looping is nested and only one of the cases can pass through this if condition.
